national.title: Israel's election results are in. Here's what could happen next
national.summary: Israeli election results are in, showing the makeup of the country's next parliament but leaving open the question of who will be prime minister.
national.body:
Tia Goldenberg, Associated Press Tia Goldenberg, Associated Press

TEL AVIV, Israel (AP) — Israeli election results are in, showing the makeup of the country's next parliament but leaving open the question of who will be prime minister.

Party leaders will now hold high-stakes negotiations as they try to cobble together a 61-seat coalition in the 120-member assembly, known as the Knesset.

WATCH: What's next for Israel after election produces political gridlock

It's a tough path ahead for both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. Neither of their camps won a majority, and Arab-led parties, which won a historic 19 seats, could play a decisive role.

Any possible coalition would require candidates to make tough compromises that could outrage their own voters. If they are unable to do so, new elections would be held early next year, with Netanyahu's government staying on as caretaker until then.

On paper, the most straightforward solution would be for Eisenkot to join forces with the Arab-led parties in a solid, 67-seat coalition opposed to Netanyahu. Even if they don't join his coalition, they could provide crucial backing for a minority government.

But that would be politically risky for Eisenkot and his Jewish allies.

national.title: Ceasefire allows evacuation from devastated Russian-occupied Oleshky
national.summary: But several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay in the frontline town, despite the lack of gas, electricity and running water.
national.body:
Hundreds of residents of the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have said, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.

"Everything unfolded without any incidents, and both sides noted the high level of organisation," Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said.

Ukrainian authorities confirmed the evacuees were on their way to southern Russia, from where they will travel on to Ukraine through Belarus.

Melania Trump said that "all elements of the convoy, including the safe passageway in and out of Oleshky, was established through mutual agreement between Russian and Ukrainian leaders".

A ceasefire - the longest and most widespread since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 - has been in force in the entire frontline region of Kherson since Tuesday, allowing for the road out of Oleshky to be demined.

Residents who wished to leave had a four-hour window to do so on Friday. A convoy of 25 buses was brought in to allow up to 750 people to leave the town until 14:00 (12:00 GMT), along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.

Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay, despite the widespread devastation and the lack of gas, electricity and running water.

"Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to do so safely," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Friday morning.

national.title: Campaign texts, powered by AI: How new tech is shaping voter outreach

national.title: A historic vote born of fear and frustration for Palestinian citizens of Israel
national.summary: Large segments of Israel's Palestinian Arab minority have historically stayed home and not voted in the country's elections. But they turned out in record numbers this week, reflecting a desperation that outweighed any qualms about participation.
national.body:
SAKHNIN, Israel (AP) — For Palestinian citizens of Israel, it was a rare moment of political triumph.

Hundreds of thousands voted in record numbers, giving two Arab-led parties their largest-ever number of seats in Israel's parliament.

Many boycotted past elections, seeing little point. But after years of their communities being demonized or neglected, some of Israel's most marginalized citizens turned to the ballot box to fight back against the most right-wing government in the country's history.

"We are here and we're not on the sidelines," declared Mansour Abbas, leader of the Ra'am party, as supporters cheered in a wedding hall Tuesday night, watching the exit polls.

WATCH: What's next for Israel after election produces political gridlock

The surge makes them a major political force that could enable opposition parties to assemble a coalition to oust Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

But the question is whether Netanyahu's main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, and other opponents will ally with them. Only once has an Arab-led party ever served in an Israeli government. During the campaign, Netanyahu had accused his main opponents of planning to form a coalition with them, which Eisenkot denied.

Netanyahu and his allies are now turning up the anti-Arab rhetoric even further, making unproven claims that foreign powers bribed voters to back Arab-led parties. In a Thursday post on X, Netanyahu warned against any party forming a government with them, saying it would lead to the "Islamization of Israel."

national.title: Last independent newspaper in Russia forced to shut down
national.summary: The editor of Russia's last independent newspaper, Novaya Gazeta, says Vladimir Putin's government has "forced the editorial team to stop its work."
national.body: Novaya Gazeta, Russia's last independent newspaper, announced Friday that it will cease operations from Nov. 9, marking a major milestone for President Vladimir Putin's years-long effort to silence the country's free press.Novaya Gazeta said it was being forced to close under pressure from Russian authorities and security services. "The newspaper no longer exists," editor in chief Sergei Sokolov said in a video statement shared Friday on YouTube. "The Russian government, Russian special services, forced the editorial team to stop its work."The announcement came a day after the newspaper's staff learned they were being evicted from their Moscow newsroom on Potapovsky Lane, where journalists had worked for nearly 30 years. At the same time, the system that enabled readers to donate to the paper was switched off, cutting its only remaining source of funding. The Anna Politkovskaya Museum, a memorial to the paper's renowned investigative journalist who was shot dead two decades ago, will close with the newspaper, as it has been housed in her former office.Sokolov said authorities had left the team no choice but closure. In his statement he said the newspaper's staff would now "end on the street, with no means of subsistence and under the constant threat of repression." Novaya Gazeta was founded in 1993 with money donated by former Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, from his Nobel Peace Prize award. It became the standard-bearer for investigative reporting in post-Soviet Russia, exposing corruption and human rights abuses, including Politkovskaya's reporting on the war in Chechnya. national.title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up 'confused and in pain' after failed execution
national.summary: It is Pike's first public statement since she survived an execution attempt by lethal injection in September.
national.body:
US death row inmate Christa Pike has released her first public statement since her botched execution in September.

"There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain," she said in the statement.

"My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn't just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul."

Pike, 50, was discharged from hospital at the end of last month after surviving two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital, which left her in a critical condition.

She has since been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

Pike is thought to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's

Published 2 October I interviewed Christa Pike 20 years ago - I can't stop thinking about her

national.title: Medline electric beds pose fire hazard after 2 deaths, FDA warns
national.summary: The medical equipment supplier's motorized beds can overheat and cause fires, regulators said in an urgent alert to consumers.
national.body: The Food and Drug Administration is warning that electric hospital beds from medical equipment supplier Medline can pose a fire hazard, after two people died and another 16 users were seriously injured. Medline, based in Northfield, Illinois, issued an "urgent" safety notice this week instructing customers to discontinue using its beds and other products without first modifying them. The company's hospital beds use built-in electric motors and remote controls that an operator can use to adjust a patient's position for treatment. Medline said that under certain conditions, including when their motors or other components jam, the beds' electrical components can overheat, leading to smoking, melting, burning and fire. "Overheating of the bed's electrical components may progress to smoking, sparking, melting, burning, and/or fire," Medline said, according to the FDA alert. "These events may increase the risk of adverse health consequences, including electrical shock and burns."Medline added that using the beds' accessories can pose a risk of asphyxiation or entrapment, both of which can lead to injury or death. Medline is advising vendors to halt sales of its branded beds and related equipment, including bed rails, mattresses and bed kits.The company, which is publicly listed and has a market value of $43 billion, said it is ending production of homecare and long-term care beds and accessories and exiting the market.In an Oct. 24 press release, the company recommended modifications for customers still using the beds. A Medline spokesperson told CBS News that customers can continue to use its products in accordance with the company's instructions. Medline will also provide users with additional information about any affected products in the future, the spokesperson said.For more information, Medline customers can contact the company at 800-950-0128 (option 7).

national.title: Tech stocks crushed as Nasdaq tumbles more than 600 points
national.summary: Disappointing earnings reports from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel are renewing fears that the AI trade could unravel.
national.body: The Nasdaq Composite Index tumbled 610 points, or 2.3%, in early trading on Friday after disappointing earnings reports from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel renewed fears about the prospects for artificial intelligence. Intel's stock plunged nearly 29% once trading opened, while Alphabet shares continued to wobble after the company's Class A stock slid more than 12% on Thursday, its worst day since the company went public as Google in 2004. The drop erased roughly $500 billion in Alphabet's market value."This has been one of the worst tech earnings seasons in memory, with underwhelming results from a slew of very prominent companies," market analyst Adam Crisafulli, head of Vital Knowledge, said in a research note. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average slumped 1.2% and 0.4%, respectively, after the opening bell.The weaker-than-expected tech earnings reports are heightening concerns that massive investments in AI will not generate the payoff Wall Street expects. Investors are also worried about the debt companies are taking on to finance data center capital expenditures and whether that debt is sustainable. "Mega-cap stocks have faced increased selling pressure over the past two weeks as elevated AI-related spending and rising financing costs raise concerns over the path to profitability," Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for brokerage firm LPL Financial, said in an email. "Recent earnings reports have added to these concerns, revealing slowing growth in select hyperscalers' core businesses."Investors have been banking on the explosive growth of AI, which has propelled the stock market to record highs, to continue to dominate. However, that sentiment is now under threat. In a report earlier this week, Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, CIO Americas and global head of equities for UBS' Chief Investment Office, advised clients to "diversify beyond AI.""While we maintain a constructive outlook on the structural growth of the AI theme, high expectations and potentially wide differences in company outcomes underscore the risks of single-stock concentration," she said. "We think investors should ensure their equity portfolios are broadly diversified."

national.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
national.summary: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.
national.body:
US stocks have continued to slide as concerns continue to intensify over the increasing costs of the artificial intelligence (AI) build out.

Shares in Intel continued their overnight slide into early trading on Friday, falling as much as 30% after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market even as it plans to increase spending on AI.

Amazon shares fell as far as 6% before recovering after its reported earnings on Thursday evening fell short of investors' expectations.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%, as other tech stocks including Reddit and Roblox continued to fall.

Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 1% after Thursday's massive slide.

The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value after its earnings update rattled investors.

On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year, and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.

"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.

national.body: Supporters of Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola in Juneau, Alaska, told CBS News they still support her bid. Peltola is facing intense criticism over a New York Times report that operatives aligned with her campaign were involved in the Dan Sullivan recruitment effort. Peltola has denied any involvement or knowledge of the scheme. Democrat Bob Coghill said he thinks the controversy could hurt Peltola with late deciders. "I do think it will hurt her chances," Coghill said. "I think there are people that will see this as something just a little too clever, a little too untoward, and it's going to hurt some votes of the people who — particularly the last-minute voters." Carter Bancroft, an independent voter heading to vote early for Peltola, said he disliked the political gamesmanship, but questioned the push to prosecute Peltola. "Seems like a mess," Bancroft said. "Seems to me possible, probable, that he is in this race to confuse things." He added: "I don't like the shenanigans that go on on both sides, gerrymandering in a variety of ways, that it seems like politicians stump more on confusing people, in many ways, than they do on actual issues. I feel like that's possible here, and I don't like that. On the other hand, it doesn't seem — it may be tasteless if that's true, but it's not criminal." Democrat Leah Haskell-Cummins called the allegations against Peltola "ridiculous" and "fearmongering." She said the ballot clearly distinguished between the two Dan Sullivans, making voter confusion unlikely.

national.title: Difficult negotiations lie ahead in Israel after Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority
national.summary: Israel's final election results confirmed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority and that weeks of difficult negotiations among very different parties, from ultra-Orthodox Jewish to secular to Arab-led, lie ahead.
national.body:
Ibrahim Hazboun, Associated Press Ibrahim Hazboun, Associated Press

JERUSALEM (AP) — Israel's final election results confirmed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority and that weeks of difficult negotiations among very different parties, from ultra-Orthodox Jewish to secular to Arab-led, lie ahead.

The results released early Friday showed Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday's election. The main opposition bloc won 48. Arab-led parties secured the other 19, a historic showing. Now parties must meet, bargain and seek a way to team up for at least 61 seats in the 120-member Knesset.

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, remains in charge.

"Now comes the truly hard part," centrist politician Yair Lapid said on X, urging patience and adding: "If you want to know if something's happening behind the silence you're hearing now, the answer is yes."

Difficult decisions lie ahead. Will the main opposition parties that campaigned hard to unseat the divisive Netanyahu make the politically sensitive choice to partner with Arab-led ones? Or will they toss their vows aside to team up with Netanyahu in a potentially fractious unity government?

Israel largely shuts down on Friday for the Jewish Sabbath, and it was not clear who might be meeting with whom. Israelis debated possible coalitions and challenges, as some expressed traditional wariness around Arab parties and others insisted it was time for Jewish-led parties to embrace them.

national.title: A midterm crossroads for both parties eyeing the beginning of the end of the Trump era
national.summary: The nation's major political parties are at a crossroads. Win or lose Tuesday, the end of the 2026 midterms marks the beginning of a high-stakes fight over the direction of the Republican and Democratic parties as the Trump era nears its end.
national.body:
Steve Peoples, Associated Press Steve Peoples, Associated Press

NEW YORK (AP) — The nation's major political parties are at a crossroads.

A decade after he began to remake the Republican Party in his image, President Donald Trump is facing the prospect of a voter rebellion Tuesday that could force conservatives to rethink their undying allegiance to the 80-year-old lame-duck leader and his "Make America Great Again" movement. Already, some Republican candidates have begun to distance themselves from him.

And Democrats, who remain unpopular despite midterm momentum, are speeding toward a tug-of-war between establishment leaders and emboldened progressives demanding nothing less than transformative change.

Whether either party wins or loses Tuesday, the end of the 2026 midterms marks the beginning of a high-stakes fight over the country's political future in the twilight of the Trump era — a fight that will swiftly surge to the forefront of American politics as new members of Congress descend upon Washington and the 2028 presidential contest takes off.

"When President Trump leaves office, it's going to create a tremendous vacuum. And I ask the question, where does the country go next?" said former Republican Sen. John E. Sununu, who is running for the New Hampshire Senate seat he lost in 2008.

WATCH: Where key Senate races stand in the final days of campaigning

More than any policy or principle, the most powerful unifying force in the modern-day Republican Party has become Trump himself.

national.title: Democratic senator blames Egypt press crackdown on US military aid decision
national.summary: Chris Murphy said waiving a human rights condition on aid paved the way for arrests of journalists.
national.body:
A top Democratic senator has blamed a crackdown on independent journalism in Egypt on a decision by the Trump administration to waive human rights conditions on US military funding to the country.

Chris Murphy, who sits on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, accused the US government of "abandoning" the Egyptian people after it lifted restrictions relating to more than $300m of defence assistance.

Over the last month a series of arrests has taken place of journalists at two of the few remaining independent news outlets in Egypt, where newspapers and TV stations are closely controlled by the authorities.

The US State Department told the BBC it waived conditions on a portion of military aid to Egypt in September due to the country's "importance to US national security interests".

Murphy, speaking at the Middle East Institute (MEI) in Washington this week, said he was in no doubt the two were linked.

"The minute that money was released, the crackdown began in an absolutely devastating way," he said.

On Tuesday a court in Cairo ordered the closure of the news website Madr Masa and fined its editor-in-chief Lina Attalah in what Amnesty International called "a crushing blow to press freedom".

Earlier this month, authorities arrested six journalists at the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh and charged them with belonging to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.

national.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election
national.summary: The PM's Likud party has alleged foreign interference and said Arab-led parties "stole" the election after his coalition lost its majority.
national.body:
The main Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab-led party leaders have denounced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleging foreign interference following the election which saw his coalition lose its majority.

Netanyahu's Likud accused Israel's Arab-led parties of "stealing" the election. Home security agency Shin Bet is investigating whether they received illegal funding from Qatar and Turkey.

Qatar's foreign ministry denied the "ridiculous and dangerous" allegations and accused Israeli politicians of conducting a disinformation campaign against Doha.

Final results confirmed that neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the Jewish opposition had won a majority in parliament.

The two Arab party lists - The Joint List and the Ra'am - defied expectations to win a record 19 seats in the 120-seat Knesset following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers, with Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats and his rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc securing 48.

According to protocol, the president will appoint a party leader whom he believes has the best chance to form a majority government. That leader has up to 42 days to achieve this, before the task passes to a second nominee who is given 28 days. If that nominee is unsuccessful, a period of 14 days is granted to a third candidate, after which, if no government has been formed, new elections will be called.

On Thursday Likud alleged that voters had been "bribed" to vote for Arab parties, after the head of the Central Elections Committee (CEC) asked the Shin Bet security service to investigate "serious suspicions" of foreign interference.

national.title: Meteorite found in the Sahara Desert turns out to be piece of Mars
national.summary: A meteorite found in the Sahara Desert has been determined to be 4.1 billion years old and from Mars.
national.body: A rose-colored meteorite found in the Sahara Desert in 2022 has been identified as a 4.1-billion-year-old chunk of the Red Planet, a NASA study determined. The nearly two-pound meteorite was found in Mali. It was named Teghaza 001, after the salt plain where it was discovered, NASA said in a news release. Study of the meteorite allowed NASA scientists to determine it was one of roughly 435 from Mars. Meteorites can be verified as having been part of Mars by comparing their chemical and mineral makeup to samples and data collected by NASA's Martian missions. Age-dating of the meteorite led researchers to conclude it was about 4.1 billion years old, making it one of the three most ancient Martian meteorites found on Earth, NASA said. That provides "a rare snapshot" of the planet's crust and formation, the agency said. "It was only after we started looking closely that we realized this meteorite is really unique," said Yang Liu, the lead author of a paper detailing the age-dating process and related discoveries. Liu is part of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. "One of the paper's reviewers called it a Rosetta Stone for Mars." Previous ancient Martian meteorites provided narrower glimpses into the planet's history. But Teghaza 001 shows how Mars' crust formed from cooling magma and was then changed by water on the planet's surface. The meteorite is made of a unique mix of volcanic minerals, including zircon crystals, NASA said, matching samples observed by the agency's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter in the planet's southern highlands. Francis Tissot, a geochemistry professor at Caltech, helped the researchers use a pioneering age-dating method that studied a piece of meteorite smaller than a fingernail. The precise method allowed scientists to analyze single grains of minerals. That analysis showed the rock had been altered by Martian water about 4.1 billion years ago. The rock itself may have been formed even earlier, NASA said. The data also showed that early Mars may have had a more dynamic water cycle than scientists previously believed. national.title: Six dead after helicopter crashes in northern Indian state
national.summary: The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.
national.body:
Five pilgrims and a pilot have died after their helicopter crashed in the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand, officials say.

The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.

The cause of the crash is not yet known but there had been reports of heavy rain and poor visibility in the region.

Uttarakhand, a Himalayan state which borders China and Nepal, is home to some of Hinduism's holiest shrines and attracts millions of pilgrims every year.

Badrinath is one of four sacred sites on the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit, alongside Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri. Many devotees travel through steep Himalayan valleys to reach the temples, which are open for only part of the year because of harsh winter conditions.

Uttarakhand's Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the helicopter came down near a village close to Joshimath in Chamoli district.

national.title: Spain transport minister says he won't resign over high-speed rail disaster
national.summary: Óscar Puente has been facing calls to resign after two high-speed trains collided earlier in the week, killing at least 69 people.
national.body:
Spain's transport minister says he won't resign over the high-speed rail collision that has left at least 69 people dead.

Óscar Puente told a news conference in Madrid he had "nothing to hide" while repeating the government's vow to get to the bottom of the disaster, saying many questions needed to be answered.

"My duty right now is not to talk about whether I should remain in my position, but to resolve the problem," Puente said.

The transport minister has been facing calls to step down in the aftermath of the tragedy, including from political rivals, a trade union and demonstrators who protested outside the transport ministry on Wednesday night.

Dozens were killed and many more injured when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of another stationary train operated by the Iryo company near the town of Urda, in the central Toledo province, on Wednesday morning.

A preliminary report released by transport investigators late on Thursday found the Renfe train was travelling between 160km/h (99.4mph) and 200km/h when the collision occurred, causing its front carriage to become embedded in the tail of the stationary train.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said earlier on Friday that public trust in Spain's high-speed rail network had been broken and repeated it was "unacceptable" that there had been two similar tragedies within a year.

In January a collision on the same Madrid-Seville route killed 46 people in Adamuz in southern Spain.

national.summary: The Chicago-born pontiff, who has a tense relationship with Trump, mailed in a ballot for the midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress.
national.body:
Pope Leo XIV has submitted his mail-in ballot in Illinois, for the midterm elections, becoming the first-ever pope to vote in a US election.

"The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes," the Holy See Press Office said in a statement.

The Chicago-born pontiff is the first US citizen to hold the Vatican's highest seat, after his selection in May 2025.

Since then, he has clashed with the Trump administration over various issues, including immigration enforcement and the US-Israel war with Iran.

"Pope Leo XIV has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so," the press office said, including during his years in Peru.

The US midterm elections will determine which political party controls Congress and have a significant impact on the final years of Donald Trump's presidency.

Elections will be held nationwide on 3 November, but early voting has begun in most states.

According to NBC News, the Pope requested his mail-in ballot from the Will County Clerk's Office on 3 October.

national.summary: Early voting is continuing to significantly outpace the last midterm election, with millions more Americans casting ballots in advance and particularly sharp increases in states hosting competitive Senate races, according to an Associated Press analysis of voting data five days before Election Day.
national.body:
Joey Cappelletti, Associated Press Joey Cappelletti, Associated Press

Simran Parwani, Associated Press Simran Parwani, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — Early voting is continuing to significantly outpace the last midterm election, with millions more Americans casting ballots in advance and particularly sharp increases in states hosting competitive Senate races, according to an Associated Press analysis of voting data five days before Election Day.

The surge is especially pronounced in Texas, where voters are deciding closely watched Senate, House and governor's races. More than 6.3 million Texans had voted early as of Wednesday, compared with 4.2 million at the same point four years ago, a 50% increase.

Advance voting has also increased more than 30% from the same point four years ago in Maine, Michigan, North Carolina and Kansas, states with competitive Senate races. In South Carolina, where voters are choosing a successor to the late Republican Sen. Lindsey Graham, early voting is up 83%.

WATCH: Democratic and GOP strategists assess midterm landscape in final week

The data, compiled by the AP, offers a glimpse of early voter participation five days before an election that will determine control of Congress and other key contests.

Across the country, more than 43 million Americans had voted early in person or returned mail ballots, nearly 10 million more than in 2022. The figures cover 47 states and Washington, D.C., compared with 48 states and the nation's capital four years ago.

LOS ANGELES (AP) — Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it's investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident "does look like a hack on Binance." national.title: Alaska Senate candidate denies knowing about alleged plot to put two Dan Sullivans on ballot
national.summary: Dan S Sullivan, the incumbent Republican senator running for re-election, and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters by recruiting Dan J Sullivan to also stand in the race.
national.body:
Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola has denied she knew anything about an alleged "scheme" that led to two men named Dan Sullivan standing in the Alaska Senate race.

The denial comes as the Trump administration continues to escalate a criminal investigation into the matter, according to US media. The Republican governor of the state ordered an official inquiry earlier this week.

Dan S Sullivan, the incumbent Republican senator running for re-election, and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters.

The Alaska race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest of the upcoming US midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress.

"I just want to clear the air," Peltola said while speaking to voters on Thursday. "I knew nothing about any other candidate on the ballot except for me and the incumbent. That is all I have ever known about. I am not interested in tricking voters."

Both Dan Sullivans have been running for the open Senate seat for some time. Still, controversy erupted earlier this week when The New York Times , external reported that Peltola's team worked with people who tried to recruit spoiler candidates in the Senate race.

The Times's report alleged that people connected to Peltola's campaign, as well as senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), worked to try to recruit Dan J Sullivan, a retired teacher who lives in a remote fishing village, to stand in the Senate race.

The paper said it had seen text messages and interviewed 12 people who participated in or were told of the plan, or were would-be candidates who the team tried to recruit. The BBC has not independently verified the reporting.

The Dunkirk Police Department released information Friday about a series of incidents involving juveniles.

"Over the past several months, the Dunkirk Police Department has observed a significant and concerning increase in incidents involving juvenile offenders throughout the city of Dunkirk," the release stated. "These incidents have included trespassing, burglaries, theft, assaults, threats involving weapons, and other criminal activity. In several of these cases, juveniles have also physically resisted responding police officers."

The department described seven incidents since Sept. 24. Four of them involved physical violence against other people, or the threat of it. Here are the four incidents:

-- Sept. 24: Officers located a 13-year-old female and a 15 year-old female trespassing inside a school building. When confronted by officers, the 13-year-old refused to leave after being directed to do so and subsequently resisted officers. She also threatened a school staff member.

The 13-year-old was petitioned to Family Court on charges of third-degree criminal trespass, resisting arrest, second-degree obstructing governmental administration, and second-degree harassment. The 15-year-old was petitioned to Family Court on a charge of second-degree criminal trespass.

-- Oct. 10: Officers responded to an address for a reported home invasion. During the incident, one of the residents was allegedly stabbed. Investigation involves several juvenile suspects remains ongoing.

-- Oct. 24: Officers responded to a local business for a reported menacing incident. The business owner reported that a 15-year-old juvenile had tampered with property inside the business and, when confronted, threatened the owner with a knife.

The juvenile was petitioned to Family Court on charges of second-degree menacing and third-degree criminal tampering.

local.title: Healthy Baby Network reflects on 30 years of service
local.summary: The Healthy Baby Network is celebrating 30 years serving the Rochester region. The pregnancy care organization works to provide resources for birthing parents and families affected by inequitable access to healthcare.
local.body:
The Healthy Baby Network is celebrating 30 years serving the Rochester region.

The pregnancy care organization works to provide resources for birthing parents and families affected by inequitable access to healthcare.

The CDC estimates 80 percent of the maternal deaths due to pregnancy-related complications are preventable and Black women are three times more likely to die.

Sharita Bullock is the president and CEO of Healthy Baby Network . She says the organization's focus now is on the next 30 years to improve birthing outcomes for both parents and babies.

"We can't keep doing what we have been doing," Bullock said. "What we have been doing has gotten us to where we are, and when we agree that it's not acceptable for us to have preventable deaths, then we need to bring like all of our best thinking together."

A major focus has been the transition from its start as a systems integration organization to providing direct services to families. Bullock says partner organizations have been key in making sure parents are healthy so that babies can be born and live healthy lives.

"As parent and infant health has evolved and the challenges that parents are facing have evolved, it's required us as an organization to also evolve while we maintain those things that are super great about how we work and how we work together, as well as prepare and rise and meet the challenges and circumstances that we know our parents are navigating," she said.

Among the organization's most successful initiatives, Bullock includes the NEST program which centers on raising families out of poverty. It provides pregnancy education, preparation, and a $1,000 monthly incentive for parents to consistently meet with their case workers.

local.title: New York state comptroller candidates offer differing outlooks
local.summary: State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli is facing a challenge from New York City businessman Joseph Hernandez in his bid for re-election.
local.body:
State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli , currently the longest-serving statewide official, is making the argument that experience counts as the Democrat seeks re-election.

But his Republican opponent, New York City businessman Joseph Hernandez , says DiNapoli hasn’t done enough to combat fraud and abuse in state government during his 19 years in office. And that the state pension fund is underperforming.

The comptroller oversees the fund and serves a watchdog function over the spending of state and local tax dollars.

“When you look at the performance of the S&P, for example, last quarter the S&P generated about 15% return,” Hernandez said during their only debate, which was televised by Spectrum News NY1. "Nasdaq generated 21%. So when you say you did well at 6.2%, that's not the full score.”

“I've tried very hard to de-risk the fund as best as possible to provide that retirement security,” DiNapoli said during the debate. “We have an assumed rate of return of 5.9%, one of the lowest in the country. It means we don't have to take risky bets because there are market cycles.”

DiNapoli first took office in 2007, elected by the Legislature after the resignation of then-Comptroller Alan Hevesi. DiNapoli said he’s prided himself on cleaning up the office and rooting out fraud in state government.

“I want to continue our audits and our investigations to make government more cost-effective, reduce costs to our taxpayers, and hold wrongdoers accountable,” he said.

He highlighted the office’s work on Medicaid, citing 55 arrests and $44 million in recovered funds since 2023.

local.title: Brighton district to update community on athletic field project and cleanup
local.summary: The Brighton Central School District is again moving forward with plans to build an athletic field behind its high school. But first, soil and air in the area are being tested for contamination.
local.body:
Listen • 1:18 The Brighton Central School District is again moving forward with plans to build an athletic field behind its high school. But first, soil and air in the area are being tested for contamination.

The district put the turf field project on pause in March after soil contamination was discovered by a contractor. Now, it's moving forward with a cleanup so it can resume construction of the field behind the high school.

The cost of that work is about $3 million according to an Interim Site Management Plan published in May.

According to that document, an alternative approach to remove all contamination, or "historic fill materials," would amount to more than 15 million dollars. Fill materials in this case refer to cinder, ash, glass, brick, metal and ceramics buried up to seven feet below the surface. Mercury and cyanide were also detected in soil samples taken earlier this year.

The district has scheduled a community forum at 7 p.m. Nov. 17 at the Administrative Building, 2035 Monroe Ave. State Department of Environmental Conservation representatives and the district's environmental consultants are expected to attend to answer residents’ questions.

local.body:
No one needs to explain to New York gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman that he and his team need to run hard through the tape on Election Day. They're doing that.

Hence the Oct. 28 whistle-stop tour across the Southern Tier from Owego to Elmira to Hornell to Olean to Lakewood.

Not every candidate can be passionate without being--or at least coming off as--angry.

It would be rare for a red candidate to be the favorite in a statewide election in a dark blue state such as New York, especially when the president is a Republican, no matter who the president is.

Everyone should know Blakeman isn't the favorite. Yet under the circumstances--principally an unpopular incumbent and a state that's in trouble--Blakeman can win.

If those who are with him on issues vote for him in a big turnout.

New York has 62 counties. Blakeman will win more than 50. To prevail statewide, however, he needs to win them overwhelmingly with a big turnout.

Just to pick an extreme example, it won't cut it for him to win Chautauqua County with a low turnout and a percentage of the vote in the low 50s.

local.title: Judith H. Haynes
local.summary: Judy was the embodiment of love and kindness. Her warm smile, sense of humor, and loving […]
local.body:
Judy was the embodiment of love and kindness. In every role she held, she truly searched for a way to make the day a little brighter, or to make life a little less heavy for everyone she encountered- always putting the needs of others before her own. Her warm smile, sense of humor, and loving heart carried her through her final years as she relished reminiscing with schoolmates, friends, caregivers and family.

As a young woman, Judy enjoyed attending the Westfield Presbyterian Church as a member of the choir, and was active in the Columbine Crown Chapter of the Order of the Eastern Star where she was the flag bearer. Additionally, Judy was a gifted knitter and spent many years bowling in the Barcelona Lanes League where she was recognized for high game and high series achievements.

Judy entered the work force in 1959 following graduation from Westfield Academy and Central School, beginning a lengthy career as a Dental Assistant in the Jamestown and Westfield areas with Drs. Carstensen, Johnson, Militello and Scholl. She married her husband of 42 years, the late Richard Haynes, in 1966 and they welcomed their first daughter Melinda a year later, followed by Elizabeth in 1970, and Suzanne in 1971. Her family was her entire world, and she worked tirelessly to provide a loving home.

Later, Judy's career journey brought her to the Brocton Central School district, Johnson's Adult Home as a care giver and finally as a wellness leader at the WCA Home in Fredonia, NY where she led the ladies through crafting activities, chair yoga and cultural outings at Fredonia State College. Valuing each client as though they were family, Judy stated that she cared for them the same way she hoped to be honored when she became their age. As the cafeteria MOM-iter at Brocton Central, Judy cherished each student as she would her own child, complete with chin wiping and spill management. She loved the extra opportunity to see her kids and friends in the middle of the day, always ready with a smile and a warm hug for anyone who needed it. Those were some of her favorite years, and she always spoke fondly of the many youngsters who created a memory and left an imprint upon her heart. You all know who you are, and we thank you.

Judy is survived by her daughters, Elizabeth and Suzanne, her siblings, Elaine, Merillee, Leslie, Bill and Jon, sister-in-law, Anita, brother-in-law, Orlin, numerous Grand and Great-grandchildren, nieces and nephews, all of whom she loved so dearly. She is pre-deceased by her daughter, Melinda, husband, Richard, brother, Robert, sisters-in law, Florence and Jean, mother, Margaret Burlingame Miller and father, Howard M. Jones.

local.body:
MILWAUKEE (AP) -- Milwaukee could come to a standstill as fans celebrate the Brewers’ first World Series title.

Thousands of fans are expected to line the streets for a victory parade on Friday, forcing the state’s largest school district in Milwaukee to close because of operational and safety concerns.

The small-market Brewers gave their long-suffering fans the title they had been waiting for with a 4-1 win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday, clinching the series in five games.

Thousands of Brewers fans filled the Trop -- nearly outnumbering Rays’ fans -- and celebrated from the stands after the final out. Thousands more celebrated back in Milwaukee, where the party will continue with Friday’s parade.

Milwaukee Public Schools canceled classes on Friday, allowing fans to enjoy the parade that will run through downtown and conclude with a fan fest at Henry Maier Festival Park, not far from the shore of Lake Michigan.

Michael Maxwell, the presiding judge in neighboring Waukesha County, declared Brewers attire will be formally considered “in compliance with professional decorum expected of courtroom staff, litigants and attorneys appearing before the court” through the conclusion of the victory parade.

One fan who joined the queue to get tickets for the rally at American Family Insurance Amphitheater said he was behind 34,000 people -- at 8 a.m.

A large police presence is expected for the parade to handle the big crowds and heavy traffic.

local.title: Another impeachment is a mixed result
local.summary: A coalition of right-wing organizations and activists is lobbying the White House to grant mass pardons to junior staffers in the administration. “A pardon for all junior administration personnel is viewed as unlikely,” one source told the Washington Sun, “but the president could issue blanket pardo
local.body:
A coalition of right-wing organizations and activists is lobbying the White House to grant mass pardons to junior staffers in the administration. “A pardon for all junior administration personnel is viewed as unlikely,” one source told the Washington Sun, “but the president could issue blanket pardons for all employees involved in particular policy areas, such as deportations, war or trade.”

There’s a raging debate within the Democratic Party, mostly beneath the surface, about whether President Trump should be impeached for a third time. It’s relevant because the Democrats are almost guaranteed to win back the House, and therefore the power to impeach.

But the debate isn’t over whether Trump has done anything impeachable. That question is settled: Of course he has. Democrats are debating whether it would be politically wise to stir up all the drama only to inevitably fail at securing the two-thirds vote requirement for conviction in the Senate. Spending the next two years on a failed impeachment wouldn’t fulfill their promises to deal with “affordability” and the like.

I don’t really care about the politics one way or another. But if Democrats decide to go down that path, Trump’s abuse of the pardon power would be a good place to start.

There’s ample evidence that various figures have outright bought pardons, or received them in trade for political services rendered. If you don’t think that’s impeachable, take it up with James Madison, who insisted that a president handing out pardons in exchange for nefarious activity done on his behalf would be impeachable. You know, like sitting back as the Capitol is ransacked after your efforts to steal an election fail. Then again, Trump was already impeached for that, and the Senate refused to convict him.

And that’s the problem. Hyperpartisanship has nullified the impeachment power. If Jan. 6 wasn’t enough, what’s the point of trying again?

There are only two relevant replies to that question: If impeachment is in the political interests of the opposition party, and if it’s the right thing to do whether or not it’s in their interest.

I can come up with several more candidates for reasons to impeach Trump because it’s the right thing to do. Whether it would be in the political interest of the Democrats is a much tougher question to answer. It depends in part on the specific abuses and on the evidence. But it’s not obvious to me that any evidence would be compelling enough to get roughly half the GOP Senate caucus to convict, and that’s assuming the Senate would even take up the impeachment in the first place. That would depend on whether Democrats take the Senate.

local.summary: ORCHARD PARK — Josh Allen can appreciate how heated discussions can get over bar stools, on talk radio and social media over whether he or Lamar Jackson are the better quarterback. It’s a debate that has raged since the two were selected in the first round of the 2018 draft. Just don’t ask him to […
local.body:
ORCHARD PARK -- Josh Allen can appreciate how heated discussions can get over bar stools, on talk radio and social media over whether he or Lamar Jackson are the better quarterback.

It’s a debate that has raged since the two were selected in the first round of the 2018 draft. Just don’t ask him to take sides, even as Allen has an opportunity to move the needle Sunday when the AFC East-leading Buffalo Bills (5-1) host Baltimore Ravens (4-3).

“He’s been one of the best if not the best quarterback. And what he’s consistently done when he’s on the field is unbelievable,” Allen said of Jackson. “He’s a very special player and I’ve got so much respect for him.

“That’s why you play this game is to have matchups like this.”

Though the quarterbacks are 2-2 in head-to-head regular-season meetings, Allen is 2-0 in the playoffs. Jackson, meantime, has the edge in being a two-time NFL MVP versus Allen winning the honor once.

Refreshed from a bye week off, Allen is expected to be on the field Sunday. The question is Jackson’s status, as the quarterback resumed practicing after missing the past three outings with an ankle injury.

The Ravens can certainly use a boost after losing two straight, including a 35-13 loss to Cincinnati in which Baltimore squandered a 13-0 halftime lead.

“We have to pick each other up to move on to the next one and get that one, because we need a jumpstart,” wide receiver Zay Flowers said before noting that spark could come in the form of Jackson back behind center.

local.title: 'Decades in the making': Location of new Buffalo Animal Shelter unveiled
local.summary: The site of a vacant police precinct in Buffalo's Old First Ward will now become the city's brand-new animal shelter.
local.body: The site of a vacant police precinct in Buffalo's Old First Ward will now become the city's brand-new animal shelter.The parcel at 294 Louisiana Street was once used to train police canines. In a nod to its past, it will now house Buffalo's four-legged friends in its new lease of life as the city's animal shelter. Though the final design process has yet to take place, Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan said the shelter will be a revamp of its existing structure, four times bigger than the current facility on Oak Street. The shelter will have capacity to house around 100 dogs and between 90 and 130 cats, according to the mayor's office. The former shelter was designed to hold 66 dogs and 59 cats and is often over capacity, with a 2024 7 News I-Team investigation revealing the poor conditions at the facility. WATCH: 'Borderline abandoned': Conditions, care of animals called to question at City of Buffalo animal shelterThe Louisiana Street site was selected with help from a committee of Buffalo Animal Shelter volunteers. "Today marks a milestone decades in the making," said Kelly Gorman, who is on the committee. "Cats will be able to see daylight from their kennels and stretch their legs in community cat rooms. Dogs will have opportunity for exercise in multiple large play-yards." The new facility will be a $30 million capital project, with the site chosen for its access to the nearby green space of Father Conway Park and transportation links.But could there be trouble ahead in getting funding for this project? The mayor needs to request to borrow money to get the project going through the city's capital budget, and that's not exactly been a smooth ride over the past few years."Every project in the City of Buffalo has been delayed because of the borrowing fight with the comptroller," Ryan explained.Borrowing signed off by the common council to fund projects such as road repaving and community center repairs has been on hold after the city comptroller, Barbara Miller-Williams, questioned the amount the city wanted to borrow. That fight is still tied up in the courts more than a year after it became public.If the mayor's capital budget is approved by the council, the city plans to expedite construction to complete the project by the end of 2028.The city secured $400,000 in grants to improve conditions at the Oak Street shelter while the new facility is underway. local.title: South Buffalo neighbors divided over future of historic Eden Street brick road
local.summary: A plan to pave a nearly century-old brick street in South Buffalo is on hold after neighbors raised concerns about preserving the roadway.
local.body: A plan to pave a nearly century-old brick street in South Buffalo is on hold after neighbors raised concerns about preserving the roadway.On Eden Street, some neighbors think the red brick is an attractive part of the neighborhood, but it has deteriorated."I do love the brick, but I think it's time for it to go," Molly Griffin said. Griffin and her mother, Janie Griffin, live on Eden near Abbott Road, where they said the condition of the street is particularly rough."There's bumps all over the place," Janie Griffin said. "When the snowplows come down, you can just hear it grind. My car is constantly bumping."Jim Skrzeczkowski, who grew up on Eden Street and whose mother and sister still live there, also favors paving the street."I've always thought it should be paved over," Skrzeczkowski said. "Aesthetically, it's really nice to look at and everything, but if you're here in the wintertime and you're trying to get around, and for plowing reasons and everything, it's very difficult."Other residents want to preserve Eden Street's distinctive brick.Leonidas Longworth said he would prefer Buffalo invest in restoring historic features rather than covering or replacing them."I'd rather honestly invest in restoring the historic parts of Buffalo and bringing them back to what they used to look like, rather than tearing it all up and replacing it with something easier or cheaper," Longworth said.Some neighbors signed a petition to pave over the roadway, while others signed a petition calling for the brick to be preserved.Preservation Buffalo Niagara has since applied to have Eden Street designated as a City of Buffalo landmark, noting that the vitrified brick roadway was installed in 1928.The paving project is now paused, although crews were on Eden Street Thursday working on driveway aprons.Common Councilmember Chris Scanlon said the city wants to hear from residents before deciding what happens next."So it has been paused," Scanlon said. "Obviously, this is a public project. This is a public works project. And we want public input on it."WATCH: South Buffalo neighbors divided over future of historic Eden Street brick roadwayThe Department of Public Works is scheduled to hold a community meeting Monday at 5:30 p.m. at the Tosh Collins Community Center. Scanlon said he plans to attend, along with Preservation Buffalo Niagara."We'll have a conversation," Scanlon said.

The new representation for the women’s sports content creator also follows UTA bolstering its leadership in its UTA Creators division to get digital content makers into new lines of businesses. UTA launched its digital talent representation group in 2006 and is a leader in the space.

entertainment.title: DIIV Talks Revolution, ‘The Spirit of Rebuilding’ and the ‘Cowardice’ of Artists Who Refuse to Speak Out
entertainment.summary: After losing his home in the Los Angeles fires, frontman Zachary Cole Smith teamed up with A.G. Cook for the band's kinetic album ZIRP!
entertainment.body:
Sustaining a living as an indie rock band for 15 years, in this century, in this economy, is no small feat. But DIIV, who have seen their share of inner turmoil and ridden the waves of industry change, have not just survived. The band founded and fronted by Zachary Cole Smith is arguably in its most interesting era to date – restlessly creative and willing to challenge themselves (and us) while wisely keeping one eye on the bottom line. Consider their heavy, monolithic turn on Deceiver (2019); 2024’s hypnotic and deeply socio-political shoegaze of Frog In Boiling Water ; and now, a pivot of a different sort: candy-colored art, memorable hooks, bright melodies and wry (and occasionally hopeful) takes on the world abound on the new ZIRP! Related Selena Gomez Celebrates 'Ups & Downs' With Demi Lovato: 'I'm Proud of What We've Been Through' Meet Leah Barylsky, the Woman Behind the Camera - And On the Stage -- During Rüfüs Du Sol's Record-Breaking Tour Will My Chemical Romance Score Its First No. 1 Album Next Week (With a 20-Year-Old Album)? Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

That comic-book styled acronym of a title stands for Zero Interest Rate Policies, the post-recession cheap money that led to a handful of obscenely rich tech entrepreneurs but left many others poorer, only widening the Western wealth gap. ZIRP! ’s cover art depicts a pink, red and white distorted American flag, the stripes as arrows pointing decidedly downward. DIIV have lost none of the anti-capitalist fervor that fueled Frog , but while that album marinated in soupy polemic, ZIRP! is immediate, kinetic and singalong sweet. When guitarist Colin Caulfield holds a mock Rolling Stone with the headline “DIIV Goes Pop!” in the video for the irresistible “Trillions,” they’re only half kidding. An August announcement of the new LP trumpeted DIIV as avatars of “The New Alternative” – wait for it – “a new genre for music’s optimized VC-funded super deluxe remixed AI-enhanced algorithmically perfected wild west 2020s, where a million streams is great, a billion even better and a trillion well within reach.”

So while Smith, Caulfield, Andrew Bailey and Ben Newman are leaning into pop sounds, this is still a wickedly smart, reflexively ironic band who delivers the medicine with a spoonful of sugar.

On “Trillions,” Smith, with Auto-Tuned breeze, rattles off a wish list of material dreams that any fan of rich-get-richer capitalism might desire: gold floors, a boat, “some kind of big ol fucking plane,” adding crucially the zero-sum rot of “and I win and you lose.”

entertainment.title: Olivia Rodrigo Wears Concert Shirt Supporting Dr. Amy Acton for Ohio Governor Amid Ramaswamy Ad Controversy
entertainment.summary: "Ohio loves you, @oliviarodrigo !" Acton wrote on Instagram after the show.
entertainment.body:
Olivia Rodrigo got involved in the Ohio gubernatorial race while stopping in the state’s capital Columbus on her Unraveled Tour on Thursday (Oct. 29).

During her set at the Schottenstein Center supporting the Billboard 200 -topping 2026 album You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love , the singer donned a white T-shirt that read: “Dr. Amy Acton for Governor.” As captured in footage from the show, Rodrigo made a point of highlighting the top and giving a thumbs-up to the camera beaming images to the arena’s big screens.

Acton also took note of the gesture, sharing a photo of Rodrigo’s political fashion choice on Instagram and writing, “Ohio loves you, @oliviarodrigo !”

The pop star’s show of support comes with just a few days left until Tuesday’s (Nov. 3) midterm election, which will decide who will replace term-limited Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine. President Donald Trump has been traveling around the country in recent weeks to drum up support for Republican candidates including for Acton’s opponent, billionaire tech mogul and brief DOGE department co-leader Vivek Ramaswamy.

Ramaswamy recently faced bipartisan backlash for airing an ad starring Acton’s mother, from whom the Democratic politician has been estranged for more than 40 years after Acton’s then-stepfather was charged with raping her as a young child nearly 50 years ago, according to NBC News . Without discussing the rape case, Acton’s mother calls her daughter a liar in the ad and urges Ohioans not to vote for her.

“It’s not surprising that Vivek Ramaswamy has stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at 12 years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” Anton’s brother, Philip Stearns, said in a statement of the ad — which both Ramaswamy and Trump have stood by even as it has drawn bipartisan rebuke and been dubbed one of the most “ vile ” ads of an already very contentious, costly midterm election season. “This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core — a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants,” Sterns adds.

Rodrigo has long been vocal about her political views, particularly reproductive freedoms, which are under constant attack from conservative lawmakers. She recently raised $20 million for women’s charities via her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival, where Headcount was on site to register attendees to vote.

entertainment.title: Bobby Wright, ‘McHale’s Navy’ Actor, Singer and Son of Kitty Wells, Dies at 84
entertainment.summary: He portrayed the radio operator Willy Moss on the ABC comedy and had a country hit with “Here I Go Again.”
entertainment.body:
Bobby Wright, the singer and son of country music legend Kitty Wells who played the radio operator Willy Moss on the popular ABC comedy McHale’s Navy , died Tuesday at his home in Madison, Tennessee, his family announced . He was 84.

McHale’s Navy , starring Ernest Borgnine , Joe Flynn and Tim Conway , aired for four seasons (1962-66), and Wright appeared on all 138 episodes of the show that was set on the U.S. Navy boat PT-73 in the Pacific during World War II.

He also appeared with the rest of the cast in the features McHale’s Navy (1964) and McHale’s Navy Joins the Air Force (1966). Related Stories Critic's Appreciation Patrick Stewart's Career Was a Rare and Thrilling Marriage of the Prestigious and the Populist Movies Patrick Stewart, 'Star Trek' Captain and 'X-Men' Superhero, Dies at 86

Wright recorded for Decca, ABC and United Artists Records from 1967-79 and had 21 singles on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart, with the gentle “Here I Go Again” peaking at No. 13 in 1971.

His other singles included “Lay Some Happiness on Me,” “Everybody Needs a Rainbow,” a cover of Terry Jacks’ “Seasons in the Sun,” “Lovin’ Someone on My Mind” and “I’m Turning You Loose.”

One of three kids, John Robert Wright Jr. was born on March 30, 1942, in Charleston, West Virginia. His father was Johnnie Wright, who toured the South in an act called Johnnie & Jack, with Wells often performing with them.

At age 8, he sang with his parents on the country music program Louisiana Hayride out of Shreveport and played guitar.

He and his family moved to Nashville in 1958 when his folks became headliners at the Grand Ole Opry, and he graduated from Madison High School, where he played baseball, basketball and football.

entertainment.title: Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: In new singles like "Lake Ontario" and "51st State," the musician is speaking out against U.S. treatment of Canada: “If you have that much power, why would you not want to channel it for good?”
entertainment.body:
He never says him by name — not in the songs and not in this interview.

But there can be no mistaking who Bryan Adams is taking aim at in his recent musical output, a string of Canadian protest songs like “51st State” and his latest, the plaintive “Lake Ontario.”

Both of those songs appear on How’s It Goin’ , a Canadian concept album which drops Nov. 6 and features a dozen new tracks about Adams’ homeland. Related Stories News Russell Brand Treated Consent as "an Obstacle to Remove or Ignore," Prosecution Tells Jury in Rape Trial's Closing Arguments Movies Edinburgh Film Festival Toasts Bollywood With 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai' Anniversary Event at 2028 Edition

It’s the 17th studio album for the rocker — whose catalog of indestructible hits includes “Summer of ’69,” “Run to You” and “(Everything I Do) I Do It for You” — and easily his most politically pointed, having found a new muse in the deterioration of relations between his homeland and the United States.

Since returning to the White House, Trump has placed punishing tariffs on Canadian goods, repeatedly threatened to make Canada the “51st state” and even ordered Lake Ontario renamed “Lake America” in U.S. federal records, inflaming tensions with the country’s longtime ally north of the 49th parallel.

Adams, for one, has had enough. He checked in with The Hollywood Reporter from a tour stop in Las Vegas — he’s in the middle of a five-show run at the Wynn — to share where his head is at these days. It’s firmly grounded in the waning months of 2026, about as far as you can get from the summer of ’69.

I’ve lived in L.A. for 25 years, but I grew up in Montreal. I’m still very much a proud Canadian. And I’ve got to say, listening to “Lake Ontario,” I got a little choked up.

Wow, that’s super nice. Now wait till you hear the rest of the album.

A new showrunning team is already in place, we’re told, and will be announced soon. The writers room has been shuttered for two weeks amid the transition.

The question was, “Ironically, what innuendo-laden song is the shortest track on Taylor Swift’s album The Life of a Showgirl ?,” with the answers including “Wood,” “Anti-Hero,” “Cruel Summer” and “Karma.”

Che, who initially reacted to the question with an “uh-oh,” of course, had jokes, beginning with “Innuendo-laden? Is that a terrorist?,” to which host Jimmy Kimmel yes-and’d “You’re thinking of Innuendo Laden.”

Jost, though, went through the track length of each, randomly throwing out the totally freestyled answer, “‘Cruel Summer’ is 3:23, ‘Karma’ is 4:24,” as Kimmel giggled at the bit. “So, there’s one, that’s why I was originally thinking that it was A,” Jost said, referring to “Wood.” “I don’t want to explain to you why,” he told Che, who paused for a second and then said wide-eyed, “Oh!”

“And, I feel like the irony is, if you know some of the lyrics of the song, is talking about size,” Jost explained, showing off his Swifty knowledge while teasing out the “shortest track” hint in the clue. Che trusted his news pal, telling Jost to, “Lock it in, baby. I wood.”

As any Swiftie knows, “Wood” is the only one of the four on the album and, as suggested by the clue, it is filthy with innuendo about the impressive nature of Swift’s husband Travis Kelce’s package.

entertainment.body:
Vern Gosdin’s lonesome tone and distinctive quiver made him one of country music’s singular artists, earning the nickname “The Voice.” His run on the Billboard charts began when his Elektra single, “Hangin’ On,” edged onto the Hot Country Songs list dated Oct. 30, 1976.

In truth, Gosdin had charted the song previously, taking it to No. 37 in 1967 as one-half of The Gosdin Brothers, including younger sibling Rex Gosdin. That version’s studio band included two future members of The Byrds, Clarence White and Gene Parsons.

Written by Buddy Mize and Ira Allen, “Hangin’ On” was resurrected by producer Gary S. Paxton – who also produced Bobby “Boris” Pickett’s Halloween novelty “Monster Mash” – and recorded at Nashville’s Sound Stage in April 1976. Emmylou Harris provided female harmonies, as it rose to No. 16 on Jan. 8, 1977, launching a string of 41 Gosdin solo entries. Nineteen of them ascended to the top 10 – beginning with the “Hangin’ On” flip side, “Yesterday’s Gone” – and three of those titles reached No. 1: 1984’s “I Can Tell by the Way You Dance (You’re Gonna Love Me Tonight),” 1988’s “Set ‘Em Up Joe” and 1989’s “I’m Still Crazy.”

An Alabama native, Gosdin shared the Country Music Association’s song of the year award with Max D. Barnes for the grief-stricken 1989 ballad “Chiseled in Stone,” and saw his top 10 1982 single “Today My World Slipped Away,” co-written with Mark Wright, rise to No. 3 in 1997 after it was covered by George Strait.

entertainment.title: Russell Brand Treated Consent as “an Obstacle to Remove or Ignore,” Prosecution Tells Jury in Rape Trial’s Closing Arguments
entertainment.summary: The judge will only accept a unanimous verdict on three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of attempted indecent assault — all of which Brand denies.
entertainment.body:
The prosecution has made its closing arguments in Russell Brand ‘s highly publicized rape and sexual assault trial in London, saying his defense is “a lot of half-truths, but spun into lies.”

The jury, made up of eight men and four women, will now deliberate. The judge will only accept a unanimous verdict on each count.

As The Hollywood Reporter has covered in detail, the presenter and comedian (also star of St Trinian’s and Forgetting Sarah Marshall ) is accused of three counts of rape and three charges of sexual assault. He was initially accused of indecent assault, which was reduced to a count of attempted indecent assault by the judge on Tuesday. Six women allege offenses dating from 1999 to 2009, and Brand denies the allegations vehemently. Related Stories Movies Edinburgh Film Festival Toasts Bollywood With 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai' Anniversary Event at 2028 Edition Movies From 'Sh*t Happens' to an Erotic Photographer Being Confronted by His Daughter: Offbeat Films at Tallinn

London’s Southwark Crown Court has heard from the complainants, one of whom says she was raped by Brand in a Bournemouth hotel room after the Labour Party conference in 1999. Another alleges Brand pulled her into a nearby toilet and orally raped her at a bar in Soho in 2004 and a separate accuser says she was anally raped by the star at his Hampstead home in 2009, after the two had consensual vaginal sex. Brand is also said to have attempted to drag an MTV colleague into a bathroom at work in 2001, and exposed himself while traveling with a complainant in a car, telling her to “suck it.”

Over the last three weeks, the jury has watched police interviews with all of the complainants, whose identities have been kept anonymous during the trial. Their testimonies have been cross-examined, witnesses — including Brand’s former personal assistant, Helen Berger — have been called to the stand, and Brand himself gave evidence just this week.

He revealed he hadn’t persuaded anyone to testify on his behalf, but his wife, Laura, did take the stand on Thursday and told the room that Brand is a “caring and kind, wonderful father” to their three children. The defendant himself maintained : “I know what ‘no’ means… Consent is a fundamental, essential and necessary and in many ways more important than sex itself.”

Lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones told the jury in her closing argument on Friday that these six women do not know each other. None of them “sought the limelight” or “any kind of publicity,” she said. “None of these women has anything to gain — except perhaps some closure.”

entertainment.title: Queens of the Stone Age Finds Healing in New Album ‘Perfecth’: ‘What Has Been Shattered is Made More Beautiful by the Act of Repair’
entertainment.summary: The Californian band will perform in Mexico alongside Interpol, and will headline Lollapalooza in Argentina, Chile and Brazil in 2027.
entertainment.body:
Queens of The Stone Age turned to kintsugi, the delicate Japanese art of repairing broken pottery by filling the cracks with molten gold, to create its new album, Perfecth . By embracing this Eastern technique, the California band reflects in their new LP on the process they faced following the recent health issues and personal struggles of vocalist Josh Homme, seeking transformation through the act of repair. Related Selena Gomez Celebrates 'Ups & Downs' With Demi Lovato: 'I'm Proud of What We've Been Through' Meet Leah Barylsky, the Woman Behind the Camera - And On the Stage -- During Rüfüs Du Sol's Record-Breaking Tour Will My Chemical Romance Score Its First No. 1 Album Next Week (With a 20-Year-Old Album)? Explore Queens of the Stone Age See latest videos, charts and news

“What has been shattered is made more beautiful, not less, by the act of repair,” Homme tells Billboard Español in a video interview . “That is why the songs on this album speak about different forms of love — for family, for friends and for other people, whether significant or insignificant. There are bonds that sustain us, and others that end up breaking us.”

Homme is excited about this new work, the band’s ninth album, which led him and his bandmates (also including Troy Van Leeuwen (guitar), Dean Fertita (guitar and keyboards) and Jon Theodore (drums)) to work in different studios, cities and moments, even revisiting songs from previous sessions. Such is the case with fourth single “Run Away From the Mob,” originally recorded in 2013 with close collaborator Dave Grohl on the drums. Or “Sunday,” a track originally co-written by Homme for Iggy Pop’s 2016 album Post Pop Depression , in which the Queens frontman actively participated.

Produced by Homme and bassist Michael Shuman, this nine-track LP, released Friday (Oct. 30) through Matador Records, was born from sessions recorded in places from New Orleans to Los Angeles, achieving a production that Homme describes as “very raw, very natural sounding.”

“I think a lot of these things were played all in a room together with all the band members together,” explains the 53-year-old frontman. “And so, you want things to sound as if you are sitting in the middle of the room with us. And so, it’s very much like the ’70s, where it feels like you’re sitting in the room. And, so that’s kind of the overall sound of this record.”

The result is a dark, emotional album that goes beyond the band’s relentless stoner rock. In just 36 minutes — Queens’ shortest album to date — tracks such as powerful second single “Insignificant Other,” as well as “Where The Goth Girls At?,” “Mono,” “From The Cliff,” “Easy Street” and “Phantom Limb,” masterfully flirt with genres like art rock, jazz, folk and country blues.

entertainment.title: Jaalen Best Wanted to Be a Pro Athlete. Now He’s Playing ‘The Greatest’ Boxer Onscreen
entertainment.summary: The 28-year-old has managed to combine his love of sports and acting with his breakout role, portraying legendary boxer Muhammad Ali in Prime Video's new series.
entertainment.body:
This story might sound familiar: a rising student discovering who he is as he juggles his love for both the court and the stage.

However, this isn’t High School Musical . It’s the beginning of Jaalen Best’s trek to Hollywood, which started his junior year at East Carolina University in 2019 and led him to his breakout role, portraying legendary boxer Muhammad Ali .

After stumbling into an intro to acting class, the 28-year-old quickly caught the professor’s attention. “She would tell me how great I was at improv and how I had a face for television and I should consider moving out to a bigger city or state and pursuing acting,” Best recalls. Related Stories Movies 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' Extends Theatrical Run as Amazon MGM Says Movie "Delivered Against Our Goals" (Exclusive) Movies Sacha Baron Cohen's 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' to Stream on Prime Video Days After Brief Theatrical Stint

But he wasn’t ready to hear that yet. “I’m like, ‘I’m a basketball player. This ain’t happening.'”

Best later got another acting push from his then-girlfriend, who convinced him to audition for his hometown production of Pocahontas in Clinton, North Carolina. Though skeptical at first, he decided to give it a real shot, landing the role of Pocahontas’ father, Chief Powhatan.

“I would wake up early at 5 a.m., and I would do basketball practice for the first three hours of my day, finish classes, and then I would drive an hour and a half to my hometown and do two-hour rehearsal,” he says. Despite the chaotic schedule, Best eventually came to a realization while on stage: “I was having more fun than basketball.”

While recounting this period of his life with The Hollywood Reporter over Zoom earlier in October, Best playfully acknowledges the similarities to the beloved Zac Efron-led Disney movie, with one exception: “I wasn’t the star player. I was riding the bench and just getting my opportunity,” he quips.

Much like how Troy Bolton moved away to college to pursue his dreams, Best made the decision to move to Los Angeles post-college to follow his own.
